(Photo by Maddie Malhotra/Boston Red Sox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Something had to give with Brayan Bello in the early days of summer. After a handful of bad starts throughout the first few months of the year were interspersed with a few strong bulk appearances out of the bullpen, the right-handed pitcher absolutely imploded during a rubber game on Thursday, June 4, at Fenway Park. The Baltimore Orioles immediately jumped on him for a six pack of earned runs in the first inning. Bello eventually coughed up another pair of runs—both earned—to end with a line of seven hits and three walks surrendered across five frames. He hit one guy with a pitch, too, in case you needed any extra convincing as to how bad of a game it was for number 66. It was the straw (or, I suppose group of eight straws?) that broke the camel’s back. Bello’s ERA on the year had ballooned to 6.34 across 61 innings following that loss to the O’s, which was actually the second instance in the first half where Baltimore charged him for eight earned. He wasn’t working deep enough into games, and he had made his frustrations with that fact clear on at least one public occasion . He was adamant that his struggles as a starter (and his relative successes as a reliever) were not indicative of any trends, per The Athletic . “First of all, just stop talking about bullpen and starting games. I’ve always been a starter, and when I’ve been successful as a starter, no one asks your question (about) whether I have to be in the bullpen or starting games. So, just starting from there, just stop that talk, because I’m just having a bad season…I know that I can turn it around.” Not exactly the type of stuff you want to see or hear from the guy who figured to be playing an important role in your pennant aspirations, as evidenced by the eight-figure deal that he was given a few years ago. item.title: Offensive Coordinator targets for the Oklahoma Sooners
item.description: The first casualty of a disappointing 2026 season for the Oklahoma Sooners was announced on Monday morning when Oklahoma moved on from offensive coordinator/quarterbacks coach Ben Arbuckle after less than two seasons with the team. Tight ends coach Jason Witten will serve as interim offensive coordinator and play-caller for the rest of the season. Arbuckle and quarterback John Mateer helped the offense take a slight step forward in 2025, as the Sooners made the College Football Playoff. However, the offense took major steps in the wrong direction this year, and now Arbuckle's short time in Norman is over . With Mateer out of eligibility after this season, Oklahoma will have a new-look offense in 2027. The OU offense is in Witten's hands for the rest of this year, but the Sooners are set to have another offensive coordinator search under Venables. Simply put, Venables has to get this hire right. We're going to exclude the potential hires that aren't overly realistic, such as Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner or Texas State head coach G.J. Kinne. This list includes a variety of coaches with different backgrounds, but ultimately it's up to Venables to make the hire, which will likely happen in about a month. Here are several candidates who could be a good fit. Chip Kelly, Northwestern Offensive Coordinator Northwestern offensive coordinator Chip Kelly probably checks the most boxes in terms of what OU is (hopefully) looking for. He's a brilliant offensive mind who has been the head coach at Oregon (2009-2012) and UCLA (2018-2023) and also in the NFL with the Philadelphia Eagles (2013-2015) and San Francisco 49ers (2016). Before he was coaching the Ducks, he was the OC at New Hampshire (1999-2006), before later landing the same gig in Eugene (2007-2008). Then, he was promoted to head coach, where he rose to fame. More recently, he was the OC for Ohio State in 2024, and for the Las Vegas Raiders in 2025. He landed at Northwestern this year and is helping the Wildcats to a strong season in 2026. He's got plenty of experience, and he would not let things fall apart at OU on offense. He can also run a variety of offensive schemes, and he tailors it to what his team needs. Kelly wouldn't be the "Oklahoma" hire, but maybe that's what the Sooners need. He's got an interesting past and isn't interested in recruiting, but he'd be a candidate who could get results on Saturdays. Mitch Dahlen, Oregon State Offensive Coordinator Oregon State offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen would represent a different direction than Kelly. He's far less experienced, and he's coaching in the Pac-12 instead of a Power Four league, but his offense has been lethal this season, led by star quarterback Braden Atkinson. Dahlen knows how to coach quarterbacks, and he's followed Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer around from Fresno State to Washington to Tuscaloosa, before going out on his own this season. item.title: Shaw among big names to miss out on FifPro World XI
item.description: Manchester City stars Khadija Shaw (left) and Lauren Hemp (right) missed out [Getty Images] Eyebrows were raised on Monday when the FifPro Women's World XI shortlist was unveiled and several big names were missing. The 26-player shortlist was voted for by players from around the world and is the only award decided solely by fellow footballers. It is considered prestigious as a result but when the list dropped and five of the top 10 Ballon d'Or finishers were not included, it understandably caused a stir. Among the notable absentees was Manchester City's top scorer Khadija Shaw, who finished third in the Ballon d'Or. Malawi star Temwa Chawinga and Haiti's Melchie Dumornay were also shock omissions, along with Barcelona's Caroline Graham Hansen and Denmark captain Pernille Harder. However, England trio Ella Toone, Chloe Kelly and Aggie Beever-Jones are surprise inclusions. Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed How does the voting work? The world XI shortlist was voted for by 6,511 women's footballers from 64 countries via an online system with FifPro. The finalists are the players who received the most votes judged on their period between 4 August 2025 and 16 August 2026. All players had to feature at least 20 times during that period to be eligible for nomination and the winners will be unveiled on Monday, 9 November (13:00 GMT). The world XI will consist of one goalkeeper, three defenders, three midfielders and three forwards who all received the most votes in their positions. The remaining spot will be taken by the outfield player, from any position, with the next highest number of votes. Votes for a player in more than one position (for example, if they are named as a midfielder or a forward), are combined. Which nominations were controversial? It is not the first time the shortlists have been controversial. Last year, Arsenal and Spain midfielder Mariona Caldentey was not included in the FifPro World XI despite coming runner-up in the Ballon d'Or. In 2024, when 7,000 women's footballers voted, four of the top five in the Ballon d'Or were not shortlisted, including the often overlooked Graham Hansen. Instead, five Lionesses made the cut despite not winning a major trophy that year or having any finalists in the Ballon d'Or top 10. This time around the WSL's Player of the Year Shaw missed out. She helped Manchester City win a league and FA Cup double as their top scorer with 21 goals in 22 games. Meanwhile, the inclusions of England trio Toone, Kelly and Beever-Jones were controversial with all three initially failing to make the most recent Lionesses squad. Chelsea's Beever-Jones scored just seven goals in all competitions for club and country during the period of voting, while Toone and Kelly both struggled for form and fitness in that time. item.title: Has Georges Mikautadze made come-and-get-me plea to Barcelona?
item.description: Has Georges Mikautadze made come-and-get-me plea to Barcelona? Georges Mikautadze (26) was the subject of interest from Barcelona last summer. The Georgian centre-forward had excelled during his first season at Villarreal, following a summer move from Olympique Lyonnais, netting 16 goals in 44 appearances in all competitions. Barcelona’s sporting director Deco scrutinised Mikautadze, but following conversations with manager Hansi Flick, their interest did not go any further. Mikautadze’s start to this season has been more difficult. Despite netting five goals in all competitions, he has made just five starts in La Liga so far. The striker has admitted to L’Équipe that he is “disappointed” by the situation. However, he added that he still feels as though he is “ready to go to a big club”. Mikautadze also specifically referenced Barcelona’s interest in the summer and revealed that he is a fan of the Catalan giants. “The Barcelona interest? It is flattering and it motivates me even more. It also means that the work is done well. On top of that, since the Xavi-Iniesta-Busquets and the MSN (Messi-Suarez-Neymar), I have been a Barca fan […] but I didn’t think too much about that ,” he told the French publication ahead of Villarreal’s UEFA Champions League game against Paris Saint-Germain. Mikautadze would naturally not be opposed to a move to the Camp Nou; it is a question of whether Barcelona revive their interest and whether Flick can be convinced. GSFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: NFL Power Rankings Week 9: Hilarious Cowboys can’t even be saved by another blockbuster trade
item.description: Ah, November. The time of year when leaves turn crisp, rain turns freezing, and we start separating pretenders and contenders in the context of an NFL season. The 2026 campaign is no different. Even with Bo Nix’s Jekyll and Hyde play, his Denver Broncos somehow sit at the top of the AFC West. The Cincinnati Bengals , meanwhile, are receiving MVP play from Joe Burrow, but seem to have the same defensive issues that have plagued them since their run to Super Bowl 56. In the NFC, until or if they can find a better quarterback than Kyler Murray, it’s really hard to take the Minnesota Vikings seriously. On the flip side, if the Green Bay Packers can piece together a functional running game, they appear capable of making a lot of noise this coming winter. Then there’s the Dallas Cowboys . The Cowboys, as ever, remain a cursed franchise dedicated to inventing new ways to pull defeat out of the jaws of victory every single week. It’s to the point where we’re pretty sure another monster trade wouldn’t even fix what ails Dallas because their problems run much deeper. That might not stop Jerry Jones from making one, though. But what else is new? Let’s unpack all the latest shifts in the landscape of the 2026 NFL season in For The Win’s Week 9 NFL Power Rankings. 32. Los Angeles Chargers Last week: 32 Jim Harbaugh's offense is a bowling pin setter. An unremarkable piece of old-school machinery that does its job in a way you don't truly appreciate. Mike McDaniel came in and replaced all his bowling pins with early 90s troll dolls, and now the whole operation is failing as two incongruent systems crash into each other week after week. All the Chargers have to offer in 2026 is schadenfreude. — Christian D'Andrea 31. It came a little more than a year after his call of a Bears win at Washington set off a public back-and-forth with the Bears quarterback. That revived a perception among some Bears fans that Aikman is unusually critical of Williams (something Aikman has publicly denied). One viewer wasted little time reviving that criticism during the game, accusing Aikman of questioning everything the Bears offense did. But to his surprise, others watching the same broadcast heard a very different Aikman. Year-Old Bias Theory About Troy Aikman Resurfaces on MNF Greg Gabriel, the Bears’ former director of college scouting, wrote ahead of Monday’s game that “Aikman does not like Caleb and has always been negative towards him.” Gabriel speculated that the perceived tension began after Williams and Aikman failed to connect for their usual production meeting before a game against the Commanders in 2025. “Supposedly it started when Caleb missed a production meeting and Aikman took it personally,” he added . That meeting was scheduled for before Chicago’s 25-24 win at Washington on Oct. 13, 2025, but the two never met. Aikman’s critique of Williams that night, including his take on D’Andre Swift’s 55-yard catch-and-run, drew objections from both Williams and coach Ben Johnson. item.title: 'Certainly hasn't impressed me' - Ex-Aston Villa scout questions whether goalkeeper Zion Suzuki justifies £30m fee after Fulham blunder
item.description: Aston Villa FC v Fulham - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Former Aston Villa senior scout Bryan King has questioned whether summer signing Zion Suzuki has done enough to justify his £30 million transfer fee following a costly error against Fulham. The 24-year-old Japan international fumbled a corner into his own net during Saturday's 1-1 Premier League draw despite pulling off several earlier saves. Costly mistake mars positive start Suzuki endured his first major setback in a Villa shirt on Saturday when he dropped an Alex Iwobi corner into his own goal against Fulham. Just minutes before that costly lapse, the former Parma shot-stopper had produced a string of fine interventions, including a point-blank stop to thwart Oscar Bobb. Despite earning widespread acclaim for his reflexes and distribution since arriving in Birmingham, his display drew strong criticism. Former goalkeeper criticises extravagant style Assessing the young custodian's development, former professional goalkeeper King argued that the summer recruit still has plenty to prove as Villa's first-choice option. Speaking to Football Insider , he said: "This is a goalkeeper who makes saves look so much harder than they are, more spectacular than they are. He wants to concentrate on the simple job. He's entitled to have one good save in the game. That usually happens when you're a goalkeeper. Unfortunately, they never remember the good save. Of course he will bounce back if he's got anything about him. But as I say, he's a goalkeeper who certainly hasn't impressed me. Not for the money they paid for him." Casting further doubt over the £30m investment, King added: "I would expect the goalkeeper to come back. If he cost that amount of money, then one mistake shouldn't harm his season. But the jury's still out on him for me." Unai Emery defends Japanese stopper Despite the external scrutiny, Villa supporters and coaching staff rallied around the 24-year-old immediately after the final whistle in recognition of his strong early-season form. Head coach Emery was quick to publicly back his number one and highlight his earlier contributions during the stalemate. Speaking after the match, the Spanish tactician said: "It's part of football. We can identify and we are mature to understand we are making mistakes when we are playing. I as a coach, make mistakes everyday. Players make mistakes every match. One match in the middle of the field is not so relevant but for a goalkeeper, those mistakes are more in focus. But it's part of football and keep going forward. I prefer to speak about the saves he did." Camp Nou test awaits goalkeeper Given Emery's staunch public backing, Suzuki is firmly expected to retain his starting berth between the posts as Villa turn their attention back to European duties. Rhule spoke uninterrupted for 19 minutes before opening his presser to questions. In that time, he analyzed what went wrong against Washington, credited individual coaches and players, including offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen and quarterback Anthony Colandrea, for their effort, and pulled back the curtain on how the college football pressure cooker spilled over into his personal life. I’m not going to see my daughter shook.” — College Transfer Portal (@CollegeFBPortal) November 2, 2026 “There’s so many people that you do not want to let down,” Rhule said. “I do not want to let the fans down. I don’t want to let our players down, I don’t want to let our coaches down, but I got to go to work. What I will say, though, is this: I’m also going to fight for my family.” “My kids have grown up in coaching—and I say this for all the coaches out there,” Rhule continued. “I love our fans. But a guy walked up to my 13-year-old daughter and was like, ‘F you and F your dad.’ I’m not going to keep coaching if it means my kids grow up screwed up. I’m not going to [keep] coaching to see my daughter shook.” Rhule emphasized that he’s willing to “fight” for the die-hard fans who don’t cross inappropriate boundaries. “The guy that attacked my 13-year-old daughter, I’m not coaching for him,” Rhule said. “I’m coaching for the people that are in the boat. So, you guys can ask me whatever you want, man, but just please don’t question anybody’s integrity or effort.” Rhule doubled down on his commitment to Nebraska and its “passionate” fan base—the “grown man” who harassed his daughter notwithstanding. “I’m not leaving, I’m not quitting, I’m fighting for those people,” he said. Rhule also revealed what his 10-year-old daughter texted him. “She was like, ‘Mom had the question with us, like, is this too much for you guys?'” Rhule said. “She was like, ‘Dad, I love Nebraska, I love living in Nebraska, I love Nebraska football, [and] I love the players. Don’t quit.” The Cornhuskers named Rhule their head football coach and signed him to an eight-year contract in November 2022, shortly after the Carolina Panthers fired him . Rhule previously coached Temple and Baylor at the college level. Nebraska is 24-22 under Rhule. Nebraska (5-3) will visit the Illinois Fighting Illini (5-3) on Friday, Nov. 6. item.title: Quinshon Judkins Calls Out Browns Over ‘Self-Inflicted Wounds’
item.description: The Cleveland Browns saw their two-game winning streak end on Sunday, as they fell prey to the Pittsburgh Steelers in lopsided fashion. In the eyes of Cleveland running back Quinshon Judkins, the 27-6 loss of his team can be largely blamed on the Browns themselves. “All the self-inflicted wounds…penalties, false starts, stuff like that that we can really control…even with the field position that we have and with the defense getting their particular field position and them getting a stop and us not being able to execute is definitely frustrating,” Judkins told reporters following the game, via Camryn Justice of News 5 Cleveland . Penalties Hurt Quinshon Judkins, Browns in Week 8 Loss to The Steelers Oct 25, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Cleveland running back Judkins (10) runs the ball against the Tennessee Titans during the first half at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images The Browns were flagged for nine penalties for 85 yards and also committed two turnovers, both fumbles, with Deshaun Watson and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. committing one apiece. Cleveland racked up 319 total yards, but only managed to have 17 first downs, thanks to an inefficient 4/13 showing on third downs and 0/2 on fourth downs. Judkins himself didn’t have a great day, with the former Ohio State Buckeyes star collecting just 25 rushing yards on 11 carries. Through eight weeks, Cleveland still has a lot of adjustments to make in order to be taken more seriously. Field discipline is one the Browns can priorotize, as they are last in the NFL with 0.07 penalties a game. On the season, the Browns are also only 29th in the league with just an average of 17.4 points per game and 17th with a -0.1 turnover margin per game. The 5-3 Browns can bounce back as soon as Sunday, when they share the field with the New Orleans Saints at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans before heading back home for a Week 10 clash against the Houston Texans. item.title: NBA scouts missed Yaxel Lendeborg’s greatness with an easy mistake
item.description: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The high school class of 2020 produced one of the most hyped collections of top-ranked prospects in recent memory. Jalen Green, Terrence Clarke, and Josh Christopher were household names from early in their teenage years for mixtape compilations that drew comparisons to Kobe Bryant and other star scorers. Jalen Suggs was a two-sport stud who bypassed an Ohio State football scholarship because he was better at basketball. Scottie Barnes and Evan Mobley were portable, long-limbed defensive prodigies, and Cade Cunningham shot up to the top of the class after a stirring EYBL run that had him looking like American Luka Doncic . Yaxel Lendeborg was also in the class of 2020, but while his peers were gracing the cover of SLAM and winning international gold medals, he had yet to play organized basketball. Lendeborg’s grades weren’t good enough to get on the court back in his hometown of Pennsauken, New Jersey, and he was more interested in playing video games than applying himself to anything that would better his future. It’s possible his enormous talent would have slipped through the cracks entirely if not for a junior college on the other side of the country taking a chance on him with its last scholarship in a Covid-shortened season following an impressive weekend at an exposure camp for Dominican players. Nearly six years later, Lendeborg already looks like something close to an NBA star as a 24-year-old rookie with the Golden State Warriors. His winding journey from Arizona Western College to UAB to Michigan to now playing alongside Stephen Curry has no real analog, but it still offers some valuable insight into how prospect evaluation is changing in a rapidly evolving landscape for young players. Lendeborg is an exception to just about every rule in the sport, but his ascent is no accident, and it could inform similar success stories in the coming years for teams looking hard enough. What Lendeborg is doing to open this season is nothing short of amazing. He’s averaging 22.3 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 3.7 assists on pristine 64.5% true shooting through his first seven games. His 37-point explosion against the Los Angeles Clippers on Sunday showed the full extent of his skill set. When he was guarded by the skinnier Derrick Jones Jr., Lendeborg wielded body blows in the paint for easy scoring chances. When Brook Lopez tried to corral him in drop coverage off a pick-and-roll, Lendeborg calmly drained a pull-up three-pointer. He showed impressive body control when attacking downhill, and relentless aggression in punishing a small guard in Darius Garland on switches. With a like-sized defender in Kobe Sanders on him, he ripped mid-range shots like a seasoned pro. No rookie should be capable of this type of immediate excellence. item.title: Greatest Washington Senators: A Twinkie Town Definitive List (Round 2)
item.description: 1924 Washington Senators: Pitcher Walter Johnson. (photo by: HUM Images/ Universal Images Group via Getty Images) R1 : Walter Johnson In the biggest landslide since Ronald Reagan in 1980 , Walter Johnson was voted the greatest Washington Senator of all time. Had this been a poll for “greatest pitcher of all time”, he’d still have gotten votes. Truly one of the all-time greats. Up next: Another fleet-footed, defensive-whiz gamer. Round 2 Sam Rice (1915-1933): 2,889 H, 479 2B, 183 3B, 346 SB, .323 BA, .804 OPS, 113 OPS+, 54.1 bWAR. An outfielder who hit left-handed but threw right-handed, Rice was the ultimate speed-and-contact player for the Senators. After a stint in the U.S. Navy and a stop with the Petersburg Goobers of the Virginia League, he twice led the league in hits, once in stolen bases, and once in three-baggers. His career hit total—2,987—remains the closest to 3k of any retired player without reaching that milestone, a fact that may have kept him out of the HOF until the Veteran’s Committee voted him aboard in 1963. Perhaps best known for a controversial catch in the 1925 World Series . Goose Goslin (1921-1930, 1933, 1938): 1,659 H, 289 2B, 125 3B, 127 HR, 932 RBI, 117 SB, .323 BA, .888 OPS, 131 OPS+, 43.4 bWAR. A farm kid from New Jersey introduced to the sport via town ball, Leon Allen Goslin was given the nickname “Goose” when his penchant for waving his arms while tracking spheres in LF looked waterfowl-ish. Goose ultimately had the last laugh, winning an AL batting crown in 1928 and taking home the RBI distinction in 1924. His game was a mix of powerful contact and a little speed—twice leading the circuit in dashes to 3B. Four times he finished top-10 in AL MVP voting, and his six consecutive hits in the 1924 World Series helped the Senators nab their first title. The HOF Veteran’s Committee inducted him in 1968. A year later, severe abdominal burns from falling asleep on his couch while smoking a cigar led to Goslin’s larynx being removed and his death in 1971. Joe Judge (1915-1932): 2,291 H, 421 2B, 157 3B, 210 SB, .299 BA, .802 OPS, 115 OPS+, 48.3 bWAR. As a batsman, Judge was functional and fleet. But in an era known for shoddy defense with bad baseballs and awkward hand-wear, Judge was a consummate glove-man at the first sack. At retirement, he led the American League in fielding percentage, putouts, assists, total chances, & double plays. The kid from Brooklyn—discovered by his block’s postal worker, who gave young Joe his first glove— preserved Walter Johnson’s only MLB no-hitter with a fantastic snare for the final out in 1920. Ironically, he effectively ended the Big Train’s career in 1927 when he smashed a BP bottle-rocket into the hurler’s shin and broke his ankle. Judge died at the age of 68 in 1963 while shoveling snow outside of his D.C. home. Buddy Myer (1925-1927, 1929-1941): 1,828 H, 305 2B, 113 3B, 118 SB, .303 BA, .801 OPS, 109 OPS+, 42.3 bWAR. item.title: Grant Wolfram was fine for the Orioles
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 25: Grant Wolfram #48 of the Baltimore Orioles throws a pitch during the seventh inning against the New York Yankees in game two of a double-header at Yankee Stadium on September 25, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images Grant Wolfram came to the Orioles in April 2025 in a minor trade with the Milwaukee Brewers. He made his Major League debut at that month at the age of 28. He ultimately appeared in 21 games for the Orioles over three separate stints. He ended the year with a 5.40 ERA and mostly seemed like the kind of pitcher we didn’t need to pay much attention to. Then he made the 2026 Opening Day roster and somehow became a fixture in the team’s bullpen. He spent the entire season with the big league club and made 60 appearances, becoming a go-to lefty with the loss of Keegan Akin to injury. And while his overall numbers (4.30 ERA, 1.318 WHIP) were underwhelming, to say the least, he was a pitcher that had runs of effectiveness over the season. The funny thing about Wolfram appearing in 60 games, which was the third-most on the team after Rico Garcia and Yennier Cano, is that he was pretty unmemorable. If you asked me to name the guys in the bullpen, I’d probably get to him after Garcia, Cano, Andrew Kittredge, and Albert Suárez. But he was really a big part of the team! Wolfram made 16 appearances through the team’s first 37 games. His ERA in that span was an unsightly 4.85. It was only 13 innings, so just a blip. But not a good first impression for the season! The 4.85 ERA wasn’t really fair to him, though, as his FIP was a minuscule 0.95. If you’re not as familiar with FIP, it’s a stat that tries to remove defense from the equation when measuring a pitcher’s effectiveness. As you may recall, the Orioles were really bad on defense this year. And if FIP is to be believed, Wolfram was a major victim in the first part of the season. Across those 16 games with mismatched ERA and FIP, Wolfram pitched 13 innings, recording 20 strikeouts and just one walk. He gave up no homers, which is good, but nine extra-base hits, which is bad. His BABIP was .500(!) in that span, so he got very unlucky. I’m singling out his first 16 games because after that, on May 6th, Wolfram went on the Injured List with a lower back strain. Luckily, he needed just the minimum stay to recover and after that was healthy for the rest of the season. Upon his return, Wolfram continued to pitch well without always getting great results in the ERA column. In June he held opposing batters to a .182/.250/.212 hitting line. In July, it was .154/.303/.308. In July, he allowed his first home run of the season. But still, his ERA stayed above 4.00. In June and July combined, Wolfram had a 4.15 ERA. Nearly all of that came in a stretch of three games when Wolfram allowed six runs. Overall, he appeared in 22 games in June and July and allowed zero runs in 18 of those. item.description: Marcus Smart was at his annoying best in pestering his old Celtics squad in the Rockets' win over Boston on Monday night. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Alperen Şengün wanted one possession to prove himself. For the first chunk of Monday night's contest, the Houston Rockets doubled Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum whenever Boston brought Şengün into the action. The aggressive defense allowed the Celtics to spray the ball around and get open 3-pointers. At some point in the game, Şengün said he asked coach Ime Udoka for one chance to switch on Tatum and see if he could contain the four-time All-NBA first team selection one-on-one. Rockets guard Marcus Smart, Tatum's former teammate, gave Şengün some backup and Udoka agreed. Şengün held up quite well and the Rockets clamped down on the visiting Celtics in a 109-93 win at Toyota Center. Boston shot just 38.6% from the field and 28.6% from deep. Tatum finished with 19 points but shot 5-for-16 - he added nine assists but with five turnovers, smacking a hand sanitizer stand in frustration as he walked off the court. Jayson Tatum was PISSED after losing to the Rockets 😳 https://t.co/4wWtDCEsLE - BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) November 3, 2026 Şengün contributed on both ends as the Rockets improved to 7-1. He scored 26 points on 80% shooting and had seven rebounds, ten assists, two steals and two blocks. Only one other center in NBA or BAA history met or exceeded those numbers in a single game: Şengün against Chicago last season , per Sports Reference. "Playing elite basketball," Kevin Durant said. Smart drew multiple offensive fouls, performed his signature kip-up to get off the floor, got two steals and, even on an off shooting night, hit back-to-back 3s - sticking double middle fingers into the air after both shots. "Just a lot of pent-up emotions," Smart said of the celebration. "Plus, certain guys on the (Boston) bench was talking … so I let them hear it right back." Smart said "you always want to do good against your former team and show them that you can still go out there and do what you do." item.title: Morning Report | Darren Till reacts to missing out on Jake Paul fight: ‘It’s just a fraudulent show’
item.description: Darren Till | Photo by Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images Darren Till feels disrespected. On Monday, Jake Paul announced his return to the boxing ring, an eight-round match with MMA fighter and kickboxer Cédric Doumbé on Christmas Eve. The announcement came out of left field as Doumbé never appeared to be on the radar for Paul, and was especially surprising for Till, whose team was negotiating with Paul for the same date. “I thought we were all good to go,” Till told Ariel Helwani . “I’ve been in camp for the past two weeks with me coach. I flew him out, getting ready, seven weeks away, right around the corner. It would’ve been me third fight this year, and a big fight, as well. And out of nowhere, this f*cking daft fight gets announced with Cédric Doumbé. I don’t think anyone outside of his own household even knows who he is. “Jake probably just wants to see how his jaw’s holding up against someone who weighs about 150 pounds on a good day. So, it’s just a fraudulent show. Everyone’s a fraud. Jake’s a fraud. Nakisa[Bidarian, Paul’s business partner] is a little fraud, wasting my time. Couldn’t give a f*ck. Not arsed. If you want to fight me next year, fight me next year. But yeah. I’ve just wasted about 5,000 pounds getting me coach out here for camp and stuff like that, but it doesn’t matter. It’s all good.” This is Paul’s first fight in a year, since getting brutally knocked out by Anthony Joshua in their fight last December. Paul’s jaw was broken in multiple places after that loss and required multiple surgeries to fix, leaving him out of action for an extended period. And Till believes that in his first fight back, Paul simply wasn’t willing to take a risk like fighting him. “Maybe the fight will be there next year, once he tests his jaw against Cédric,” Till said. “Look, Cédric’s a great MMA fighter, but he can’t box, can he really? … “I’m 215 pounds. I’m the same as Jake. I can f*cking hit like f*ck. I’m not slow, I’m fast. I feel like I’m in me prime years. Everyone’s always asking me, ‘Come back to MMA.’ That could be on the cards. Every day I’m feeling better and better. … “So, I’m not bothered. As I said, I’m a fair man. But at the same time, it’s also highly disrespectful, as well. Jake, you’re just a little fraud. You’re just a little f*cking fat goblin.” Till has been chasing a fight with Paul basically since leaving MMA in 2022 to pursue his interests in boxing. That move has been productive for Till, who is 4-0 in boxing, and has also gone 2-0 in BKFC this year. And given his focus on The Sweet Science, Till is adamant that Paul simply doesn’t want the smoke with him. “Jake Paul, he’s a clear, clear juice-head,” Till said. “Look at him, mate, he’s a fat juice-head. There’s a fact for you. Cédric Doumbé’s 170 pounds. I’m not taking anything away from the guy — fantastic MMA fighter and kickboxing career. He’s not a f*cking boxer, mate. item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 26: Bobby Witt Jr. #7 of the Kansas City Royals fields a ground ball during the third inning against the Cleveland Guardians at Kauffman Stadium on September 26, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jay Biggerstaff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bobby Witt Jr was named a finalist for AL MVP. Witt, 26, joins Tampa Bay Rays third baseman Junior Caminero and Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez as finalists. The AL MVP is voted on by the Baseball Writers Association of America. Witt finished second for the 2024 AL MVP. And in 2025, he was fourth behind eventual winner and New York Yankees slugger Aaron Judge. This season, Witt hit .281 with 157 hits, 33 doubles, 18 home runs and 54 RBIs. He also appeared in 143 games while posting a 6.7 WAR (wins above replacement). Perla Paredes at MLB dot com gave an overview of Witt’s case . At the plate, Witt led qualified AL shortstops with a .281 batting average, .441 slugging percentage and 33 doubles. He also finished with 18 home runs, 94 runs scored and 157 hits while posting a .359 on-base percentage and an .800 OPS. Although his offensive numbers were more modest than in previous seasons, Witt showed greater patience at the plate, drawing a career-high 67 walks, surpassing his previous high of 57 in 2024. While Alvarez and Caminero each showcased their power with 42 home runs this season, Witt strengthened his MVP case with his elite defense at shortstop. item.title: The Chicago Bears are a legitimate Super Bowl contender
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Jeffery Simmons #99 of the Chicago Bears celebrates a stop against the Seattle Seahawks during the fourth quarter of the game at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bears picked up a crucial victory on Monday night, defeating the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks on the road, which is notorious for being one of the toughest places to play in the NFL. They were decisively the better team throughout the evening, picking up a statement 34-17 win in primetime to improve to 6-2 for the season. It was the first game in which All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons suited up for the Bears, and he certainly made his presence felt. But not only did Chicago’s major trade deadline acquisition pay off dividends on Monday, but its offense was also stellar against one of the NFL’s best defenses. Now sitting at 6-2 and firmly in the race for first place in the NFC North, it’s reasonable to think that this Bears roster really has a limitless ceiling. Here are some of my other takeaways from their win over Seattle on Monday. Caleb Williams is special Heading into Monday, no quarterback in the NFL had thrown for over 200 passing yards in a single game against the Seahawks in 2026. Caleb Williams got it done by the third quarter. He was decisive, poised, and accurate against one of the best defenses in the league, throwing for 247 yards, a touchdown, and a 101.0 passer rating. His initial 78.0 grade from the game is enough to keep him ranked No. 6 in the NFL with an 84.0 PFN QB Impact grade so far this season. The Bears felt the pressure from a very talented Seahawks defense, and that loaded Seattle defensive interior made its presence felt on passing downs and in the ground game; D’Andre Swift averaged just 2.6 yards per carry on Monday. Still, Williams maintained his composure, showing off his trademark elusiveness and sack avoidance to extend the play often and create opportunities for Chicago’s offense down the field. This wasn’t Williams’ best statistical performance of the season, but especially given the context of the situation, it was one of his most impressive. Jeffery Simmons was worth the price There was no doubting that Jeffery Simmons was going to be a massive addition to the Bears’ defense when they traded for him on Thursday. The only question was whether he would be worth the massive trade package they gave to the Titans in order to acquire him, which included two first-round draft picks. Simmons showed that he was worth every ounce of that deal on Monday night. He ended the game with six total tackles, two tackles for loss, one pass deflection, one sack, and multiple quarterback pressures. item.description: The Indianapolis Colts have already made it clear that significant changes are coming, trading two of their most accomplished veterans in Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner following the dismissal of general manager Chris Ballard. With the team now sitting at 2-6 after Sunday’s humiliating 42-7 defeat against the Jacksonville Jaguars, attention has increasingly shifted toward the future of another franchise cornerstone: Jonathan Taylor. A little over two weeks ago, I examined Taylor’s hypothetical trade value , projecting that Indianapolis could realistically receive a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 third-round selection in exchange for its star running back. That evaluation came before the Colts began moving key veterans, and with several teams now reportedly expressing serious interest, the market appears to be considerably more competitive than initially anticipated. According to reports from ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Indianapolis has been engaged in trade discussions involving Taylor, with the Denver Broncos, Minnesota Vikings, Seattle Seahawks, New York Giants and Green Bay Packers among the interested teams. Cincinnati has also reportedly entered the conversation, leaving the Colts with several potential trade partners ahead of the November 10 deadline. Perhaps the most important development concerns the asking price. Indianapolis is reportedly seeking compensation comparable to what Carolina received for Christian McCaffrey in 2022, and reports have indicated that the Colts have discussed a package involving a first-round pick and a defensive tackle. While the exact minimum price remains uncertain, I believe it will take a first-round selection, or an exceptional alternative package, to convince Indianapolis to move Taylor. That is a significant investment for a running back, particularly one who will turn 28 next season and is scheduled to earn approximately $34 million over the final two years of his contract. However, Taylor remains one of the league’s best players at his position, and acquiring him would give a contender an immediate offensive centerpiece for the remainder of 2026 and two additional seasons. Hughes is very familiar with Michigan’s rich history, and he knows the program is good at sending defensive guys to the pros. “They’ve produced many NFL-talent guys, and they’re right around the corner,” he said. “Growing up watching them, it’s a great history, a great program, so it’s kind of just me going out and being able to see it.” While visiting earlier this month for the Penn State game, Hughes got a good look at just how good this Michigan defense is. “One of the first things I saw was the stadium,” Hughes said. “I heard the stadium was big, and then I got in there, and it was huge. That was something that was nice. Just getting out there and being able to see their defensive backs go out there and play, create turnovers, get interceptions was another good thing to see.” Michigan is doing a good job staying in the race for the Rocky River, Ohio native, but he is still solid with Kentucky, as he said his commitment to Kentucky is “strong” and that the Wildcats are “like my family there, like my second family.” Ohio State is also pushing hard to flip Hughes.
